title: Stable Isotope Analysis of Feather Samples in Avian Research
author: Brian Chew
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.z2uf8ew
materials: Air duster will remove particles from chamber.
Bent tip forceps are preferred for this step.

steps.title: Prepare Cleaning Solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare the organic solvent and detergent solutions under a fume hood.

substeps.instruction: Pour 100mL chloroform and 50mL methanol into a clean 250mL beaker; stir with a rod or swirl to mix. (Optional: store this 2:1 solution in a sealable, non-plastic container of at least 250mL for repeated use).
In a clean 250mL beaker, pour 150mL deionized water and 5mL detergent, avoiding agitation that generates bubbles.
Pour 200mL deionized water into three separate clean 250mL beakers and label them '1', '2', and '3'.

steps.title: Initial Feather Measurement and Processing
steps.instruction: Measure the feather and remove the calamus for DNA preservation.

substeps.instruction: Measure feather length from the tip of the quill (calamus) to the end of the rachis or farthest barb using calipers.
Record the weight of the feather using a balance.
Using a razor cleaned with ethanol, cut off the calamus. Use a gloved hand to hold the feather base against a surface and forceps to hold the calamus to prevent loss.
Place the separated calamus into a marked, clean paper envelope; seal with adhesive and label with banding ID, location, species, sex, and date.

steps.title: Organic Solvent Wash
steps.instruction: Clean the feather using the chloroform-methanol solution.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a drying bed by layering clean paper towels.
Under a fume hood, hold the rachis with forceps and dip the feather into the 2:1 chloroform methanol solution.
Agitate the feather with stirring motions for 30 seconds.
Place the feather on a dry cloth or paper towel next to its corresponding ID envelope.
Allow the feather to dry for 24-36 hours (or until completely dry); note that 26°C room temperature near heating may reduce this time.

steps.title: Detergent and Water Wash
steps.instruction: Remove contaminants using detergent and sequential water rinses.

substeps.instruction: Using clean forceps, dip the dried feather into the 30:1 water-to-detergent solution and agitate for 30 seconds.
Remove the feather and place it into the first deionized water beaker (labeled '1').
Repeat the rinse process two additional times using beakers '2' and '3' in sequence to ensure all detergent is removed.
Place the cleaned feather on a paper towel to dry, ensuring it remains adjacent to its respective labeled envelope.
Allow the feather to dry for 24-36 hours (or until completely dry).
Place each feather into its respective clean labeled envelope and store in a separate container.

steps.title: Prepare Standards for Analysis
steps.instruction: Weight and seal standard materials into capsules.

substeps.instruction: Clean three sets of forceps and a spatula with 95% ethanol using a Kimwipe; dry under a lamp.
Clear the microbalance surface using an air duster.
Place a 3.5x5mm silver capsule (for hydrogen) or tin capsule (for carbon/nitrogen) open-end up on the balance and tare.
Using a spatula and second pair of forceps, add a small quantity of BHCO, KHS, or CBS standard into the capsule.
Adjust the mass by adding more standard or removing excess with bent-tip forceps until the required mass is achieved.
Record the mass on the data sheet and remove the capsule.

Seal the capsule by pushing the open end closed with forceps, squeezing the base flat with a gloved hand, and folding the capsule into a small, round-ish/cubic shape using forceps (repeat folding and compressing from multiple angles).
If tearing occurs or the capsule is dropped on an uncleaned surface, discard and restart.
Place the finished capsule into its designated tray well and record the position (e.g., A6) and final weight.

steps.title: Sample Feather Preparation
steps.instruction: Cut and weight the cleaned feather sample.

substeps.instruction: Clean two sets of forceps and a razor blade with 95% ethanol; dry under a lamp.
Clear the microbalance surface with an air duster.
Using a clean razor, cut a portion of the feather tip (opposite the calamus). Be consistent in the section of rachis used across all samples.
Separate the clipped rachis and attached barbs from the main feather using forceps.
Place the sample on a tared balance. Trim with a razor until the weight is within +/- 10 µg of the target mass (use barbs for fine adjustment, rachis for larger changes).
Once the desired mass is achieved, remove the sample and place it on a clean surface.

steps.title: Sample Encapsulation and Final Processing
steps.instruction: Seal the feather sample into a capsule and prepare for mass spectrometry.

substeps.instruction: Place an empty capsule on the balance and tare.
Transfer the feather sample into the capsule using clean forceps (cut sample into smaller pieces with a razor if necessary to fit).
Ensure no sample is protruding due to static electricity.
Verify the mass on the balance; if it does not match, recover any lost fragments from the balance or instruments.
Record the final mass and sample ID, then remove the capsule.
Seal and fold the capsule into a round-ish/cubic shape using the same folding and compression technique used for standards (squeeze base flat, fold, and compress from multiple angles).
If tearing occurs or the capsule is contaminated, discard and restart.
Place the completed capsule into the designated tray well and record the well position, sample weight, sample ID, tray ID, and species.
